heath@web.net did a fresh install of the 
Action applications.

The login page and add-slice page both reported
an error. 

I created a doit.php3 page that boiled the
error down.  You can see it here:

http://haumea.web.net/aa/doc/doit.php3

After perusing the phplib mailing list at

http://www.geocrawler.com/lists/4/Web/195/0/

I killed the mysql daemon with
mysqladmin -p shutdown

and then I ran 

safe\_mysqld -l -O max\_allowed\_packet=512K &amp;
-l so I could see what was going on
-O so I could set a variable that the list advised 
me to set higher.  However, this was not very 
illuminating.  Mysql was doing running the sql but
phplib was still believing there was an error.

At this point, I would say either post the problem to
the phplib mailinglist or start over with a new install
of the server -- either
a\) redhat .rpm's all the way OR
b\) source .tar.gz \(not binary\) all the way

Sorry not to get this working\!
-Michael

p.s. I've requested some mysql databases at
sourceforge, so we might be able to give you guys 
a development space there by Friday.

I'm affraid it is impossible to run APC-AA on IIS. Tested 
is just Apache \(on Linux or Windows\).

The reason, why it is impossible to use IIS is, that 
databse outputs \(slices\) are included to page by SSI 
commands. In this approach we need to get parameters from 
url to scripts included by SSI. It is problem for IIS, 
because it do not gives SSIed scripts url parameters.

Honza

\--
4.2 Creating the database
Then create your initial Action Applications database.
To do this, you need the file aadb.sql from the Action
Applications doc directory. It contains SQL commands
which create the database. When queried for a password,
use the mysql root password. 


\#  mysql -u root -p
Enter password:
mysql&gt; CREATE DATABASE aadb;
Query OK, 1 row affected \(0.03 sec\)

mysql&gt; QUIT
Bye
\# cd /home/httpd/html/apc-aa

doc/aadb.sql
